source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
Yield and financial performance data from the 250-household survey (per household, unless noted per hectare): average total land planted to corn was 3.68 ha and average land actually harvested was 3.57 ha (some planted area is lost to crop failure). Average yield per hectare was 5.99 tons/ha (range 0.335-70 tons/ha across the sample -- the extremely wide range suggests either very different farming intensities or some outlier/data-entry values).

Average total revenue from selling wet corn cobs was 8,198,663 riel per household (range 266,500-60,270,000 riel); average revenue from dried kernel sales was 10,928,377 riel (range 560,000-142,500,000 riel); combined average total revenue was 9,815,149 riel per household (range 450,000-142,500,000 riel), or about 3,470,759 riel per hectare (range 225,000-27,800,000 riel/ha).

Average total production cost was 5,880,860 riel per household (range 199,700-76,398,000 riel), or about 2,193,984 riel per hectare (range 366,876-66,700,000 riel/ha).

Average total profit was 3,934,289 riel per household, or about 1,285,551 riel per hectare. However, the reported range for profit includes negative values -- as low as -12,300,000 riel per household and -61,100,000 riel per hectare at the low end of the sample -- meaning at least some surveyed households lost money on their corn crop that season, while the high end of the range shows profits as large as 66,102,000 riel per household (25,558,750 riel/ha). This wide spread is reported here exactly as it appears in the source; it likely reflects real variation in farm scale, input cost, and yield outcomes across the sample rather than a data error, but the extreme values at both ends should be treated cautiously.
